policy.records: Samples of LibreOffice's sw/qa/extras corpus that the LibreOffice the references come from draws with a LibreOffice defect a later LibreOffice release fixed. The corpus is LibreOffice's master tree and the references come from the release reference-data workflow pins, which is older, so a sample added with an upstream fix tests that fix and the pinned release draws it the way the fix corrected.
policy.rule: While the reference LibreOffice's major.minor is older than a row's fixedIn, the checks the row names (pixel, text) are not compared for its samples: each is reported as skipped with the bug and the note that shows it, and the sample is listed under Known Reference Defects. broilerdoc still reads, dumps and renders it and has to end each in a documented exit code, and every check the row does not name runs and ranks as usual. A row stops applying by itself once references come from a fixed release.
policy.why: Ranked against a defective reference, a sample broilerdoc draws as the fixed LibreOffice and Word do stays at the top of every report: tdf163894_hidden.docx and tdf163894.docx were the first two differences of issue 170, 4 pages against 22, because LibreOffice 24.2 fills their headers with a whole paragraph. Moving the renderer toward such a reference would be moving it toward the defect.
policy.scope: A row is a LibreOffice defect, not a layout difference: the upstream bug, the commits that fixed it, the upstream test that pins the fixed rendering (or, for a fix that came with none, what pins it instead), and a reference output that shows the defect. A difference nobody has traced to a fixed upstream bug stays ranked, however likely it looks that LibreOffice is wrong.
policy.adding: A new row needs the bug (tdf#N; gerrit#N, the LibreOffice core review that merged the fix, only where the fix names no bug), the first release with the fix (major.minor), the fixing commits on LibreOffice core, the upstream tests (where the fix came with none, an empty list and an untested field saying so and naming what pins the fixed rendering instead, such as a later release's output and the producer's own saved layout), which checks it affects, every sample it covers, the evidence in prose and a repository note that shows it. The guard checks the fields, that fixedIn is newer than the baseline's LibreOffice, that no sample is listed twice and that the note exists and names the bug.

defects.evidence: The pinned 24.2 PDF wraps the three paragraphs into four pages of near-single-character lines despite a 120 cm page width. The upstream regression test asserts one page with three single-line paragraphs after widening the twip values. Local LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 also exported one full-width page.

The pinned PDF places the table on page two but clips its final rows, leaving page three blank. The 26.8 import test requires the table to flow across pages two and three with zero repeated header rows. The pinned plain-text projection retains the clipped text.

A STYLEREF field naming a character style shows the text in that style: the first stretch on the page, or the last with \l, else the nearest before the page, else the first after it. LibreOffice before the February 2026 fixes gave the whole paragraph holding the first such text instead (layout2.cxx: 'This was "Mauris ... nonummy.", i.e. full text of the paragraph'). The office-references-v2 PDFs, made by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, show it: tdf163894.docx and tdf163894_hidden.docx put their whole entry list in each header and run to 22 pages where the upstream tests pin four pages headed by single words; tdf163894_from_top.docx heads its pages with its first paragraph and runs to 5; tdf163894.fodt heads its page with the whole paragraph. LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 still draws tdf163894_hidden.docx on 67 pages; 26.8.1.1 draws four. The text projections are not affected: LibreOffice's text export leaves headers out.

A table in the body moves below a floating table that overlaps it, whatever the floating table's horizontal alignment. Before the April 2026 fix ("sw: Layout - avoid horizontal orientation check shifting down tables", no tdf bug; it finishes the TODO tdf#154775's commit 7b1c03ed left in SwTabFrame::CalcFlyOffsets) LibreOffice moved it only for a floating table aligned none, left or right, and a centred one (tblpXSpec="center") let the body table run underneath. The upstream test pins the fixed layout: no body table on page 1. The office-references-v3 PDF, made by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, draws the sample's first body table on page 1 under the floating one and runs to 3 pages; LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 does the same, and 26.8.1.1 draws 4 pages, as broilerdoc does. The fix is on master and libreoffice-26-8, not on libreoffice-26-2. The text projection is not affected: LibreOffice's text export leaves the floating table's frame out and writes the body table where the document has it.

defects.untested: The fix is part of a refactoring series ("writerfilter: move even more members to SubstreamContext") that moved the importer's per-paragraph state into each substream's own; it added no test. What pins the fixed rendering: LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 draws the sample with the heading whole, "1.3 Status Filter-Strömungstest" on page 5 and chapter 2 "Beschreibung der Räume" on page 7, and the table of contents Word saved in the document, with its PAGEREF results, numbers and places the chapters the same way.
defects.evidence: A page break run followed by a comment reference and then text splits the paragraph in LibreOffice 24.2. The DOCX importer splits a paragraph at a deferred page break when the text arrives after the paragraph's first run (DomainMapper::lcl_utext, IsFirstRun), and in 24.2 that flag was one member shared by every stream: the comment's own paragraphs, read where its w:commentReference stands, clear it. The text after the reference then starts a paragraph of its own in the default paragraph style, which keeps the heading's list at level 0 because the split erases the list id and level but not the NumberingStyleName finishParagraph copied from the heading style. Since February 2024 the flag lives in each substream's state, so a comment no longer touches the paragraph it is anchored in; libreoffice-24-8 has it, libreoffice-24-2 does not. The office-references-v3 PDF and text, made by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, show the defect: heading "1.3" alone at the foot of page 4, "2 Status Filter-Strömungstest" in 10 point body text atop page 5, and every later chapter numbered one higher (127 lines of the text projection). LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 keeps the heading whole, as Word's saved table of contents does.

LibreOffice 24.2 did not import page background bitmap fills from VML (w:background/v:background/v:fill), leaving the page background blank. Commit c14574e7ad2d3ec2ada40808be3332fac71e9767 ('tdf#126533 docx import: page background vml fill', Justin Luth) added support in LibreOffice 24.8.0, pinned by testTdf126533_pageBitmap. The office-references-v3 PDF, produced by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, renders the page completely blank (ink box blank-vs-inked, blur difference 40.89%), whereas LibreOffice 24.8+ and Word render the background picture, as broilerdoc does.

In LibreOffice 24.2, SdrPathObj::TRGetBaseGeometry failed when handling an empty polygon range, setting translation to MAX_DBL and scaling to 0. Commit 08da27fc377f443d1d6698f4a061fa462849062d ('Handle empty range correctly', Mike Kaganski, Gerrit review 167965) fixed this in LibreOffice 24.8.0, pinned by testEmptyObjectRange. The office-references-v3 PDF, produced by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, renders the page without the shape (coverage delta 0.09%, ink box delta 508 px from origin), whereas LibreOffice 24.8+ and Word render the shape, as broilerdoc does.

In LibreOffice 24.2, an unsplittable row under a repeated table header that exceeded the remaining page height reached past the bottom of the page and was truncated, keeping the document on 2 pages with dropped text. Commit f0e78f28ee6e8586d66fa8d988366a1ae02aae77 ('cool#16066 sw: omit the repeated heading where a row needs the full page', Mike Kaganski, Gerrit review 209269) fixed this in LibreOffice 26.8, pinned by testCool16066_headlineAndUnsplittableRow in layout6.cxx, matching Word by omitting the repeated heading on the page where the unsplittable row requires the full page. The office-references-v3 PDF, produced by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, truncates the row, whereas modern LibreOffice and Word render the full content. The same commit added Cool16066_addRowsUnderOmittedHeading.docx, a 10 cm repeated heading row over one unsplittable 40-line row: the office-references-v4 PDF (24.2.7.2), like a local 26.2.6.3, keeps the row under the heading and runs it past the page foot, hiding lines 33 to 40, where broilerdoc, as the fix does, leaves the heading alone on page 1 and gives the row page 2 (docs/notes/office-issue-238-docx-layout.md).

The pinned LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 PDF has four pages, three blank. The upstream fix uses automatic spacing when no line rule was specified or inherited. LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 and broilerdoc with Calibri each render one page containing all four paragraphs. The narrower fit depends on the selected font.

In LibreOffice 24.2, an out-of-order context stack pop during RTF import caused m_pTopContext to be empty when section properties were applied before a page break (\page), causing section geometry (\paperw, \paperh, margins) to be ignored or misapplied on following pages. Mike Kaganski fixed this in commit 1567f48ec9fe096da386bdaf370bc95414c8d923 ('tdf#162342: workaround out-of-order context stack pop', Gerrit 188449), pinned by testTdf162342. The office-references-v3 PDF produced by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 exhibits visual layout mismatch due to the dropped section geometry, whereas modern LibreOffice and broilerdoc preserve the specified page dimensions.

In LibreOffice, an import error during handling of a bibliography field split across paragraphs in a footnote leaves m_aTextAppendStack empty. Commit eca00082c78fddf79f247057227404738be8806c ('tdf#130214: workaround invalid state resulting from error on import', Gerrit 87595) added an early return to avoid crashing, aborting document import after the first footnote reference ('entrepreneur1'). The upstream test testTdf130214 only asserts that createSwDoc does not crash. The office-references-v3 PDF and text projections produced by LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 are truncated to 1 page containing only that first sentence, whereas Word and broilerdoc render all 3 pages and full text.

In LibreOffice 7.1, line spacing height calculation unintentionally changed to only use SwTextPortion, breaking vertical portion positioning across lines with mixed font sizes, footnotes, bidi text, and double line text (tdf#172169). Justin Luth fixed this upstream in commits 882b75b93dc25b1d4e9d42e1d18e3437fb0150d3 and 83303053d7c296db96e747fb053e76bc2a8ccf7d ('tdf#172169: line spacing height calculation unintentionally changed in LO 7.1'), targeted for LibreOffice 26.8 and verified by tests in ooxmlexport23.cxx. The office-references-v3 baseline generated by headless LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 renders with this regression.

In LibreOffice 24.2.7.2, an extra blank 4th page is generated (ink bbox: None) when endnotes contain index and bibliography sections. Modern LibreOffice (26.2+) and broilerdoc render the 3 actual content pages without the trailing blank page, with 100% semantic text projection match.

The pinned 24.2 reference PDF was generated from an upstream corrupted fixture with 466 frames and 367 phantom page anchors where text content was corrupted into a TOC section during export and ceased around page 28, leaving pages 29-30 blank with header-only ink. Upstream commit 95f32f369c14b4f76c2ea1616d2c18cc2ce4e48b in LibreOffice 26.2 replaced this corrupted fixture with a minimal test document.

Upstream bug tdf#172169 addressed line spacing height calculation regressions in LibreOffice Writer. In pinned LibreOffice 24.2, the document renders 13 pages due to pre-fix line spacing, whereas in LibreOffice 26.8 with the fix it renders 14 pages. The semantic text projection has 0 differences across all pages.
The pinned 24.2 PDFs draw both images at the top left. Upstream tests assert page-relative positions of approximately 10.5 cm for the EMU coordinate and 5 cm for the centimetre coordinate.
The pinned 24.2 reference exports Unknown; into the body. The upstream test asserts an empty paragraph because revision-table entries are metadata.

The pinned 24.2 PDF has two pages: the keep-together first row splits once and the rest of its text, from the line after pg_2 through pg_3, is never drawn, so page 2 holds only the second row. The upstream test asserts three pages whose first rows start with pg_1, pg_2 and pg_3; the text export still holds every line.

The first row of the table is marked keep-together but is taller than the 19 cm page. The pinned 24.2 PDF has two pages: page 1 clips the row at the page foot, and page 2 holds only the second row, so the rest of the first row (its last line and five more paragraphs) is never drawn. The upstream test asserts three pages ('Before the fix, the document had only two pages'). The fix landed on master and was cherry-picked to libreoffice-24-8. Local LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 exports three pages that continue the first row on page 2 and put the second row on page 3; broilerdoc draws the same three pages. The text export holds every line.

The table's first three rows carry \trhdr. LibreOffice 24.2's RTF import ignored \trhdr, so the pinned PDF draws the three header rows on page one only and leaves page two, which holds the table's empty rows, blank. The fix, committed to master on 2025-02-18 and first released in 25.8, came with this sample and a test asserting HeaderRowCount 3. Local LibreOffice 26.2 repeats the rows on page two, as broilerdoc does. The text export lists the header text once either way, so only the pixel check is affected.

The page has a printed line text grid of four lines and the document sets the MsWordCompGridMetrics compatibility flag. LibreOffice 24.2 centres the grid on the page, so the pinned PDF draws the paragraph and the grid lines about 4.4 in down the page. The fix, committed to master on 2025-02-18 and first released in 25.8, turns the centring off under Word grid metrics; its test pins the paragraph to the top of the page, as the sample's own text says it should be. Local LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 draws the paragraph at the top of the body, where broilerdoc draws it. The text export is the same either way.

A page break ends page one, and the next paragraph is an empty continuous-section mark with 200 pt of space below. The pinned 24.2 PDF starts page two with a 150 pt gap, clips the first line of the last paragraph at the page foot and puts its second line alone on a third page. The fix ('cont-sectPr w/ pgbrk == emulate bottomSpacing', master 2025-12-25, cherry-picked to libreoffice-26-2 and libreoffice-25-8) came with this sample and a test asserting two pages ('Without the fix, page 2 started with a 150pt gap, pushing content to the third page'). Local LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 exports two pages with the last paragraph at the top of page two, as broilerdoc draws it. The text export holds every line.

LibreOffice 24.2 imports DOCX endnotes without its ContinuousEndnotes setting, so it collects them on a page of their own in its Endnote page style: a default-size page with no header or footer, after the last page of the body. Word sets them right after the body text. The fix reimplemented continuous endnotes as an endnote section after the body (commit 6885dcd7, 2024-05-14) and enabled it for DOCX import (commit 1ae5ea3f, 2024-05-21); both are in libreoffice-24.8.0.1 and not in 24.2.7.2. Each listed sample has a two-page 24.2 reference whose second page holds only endnotes; local LibreOffice 26.2.6.3 sets the endnotes after the body, on one page for ten of them, and on the body's own page size with its header for tdf141231_arabicHebrewNumbering.docx. broilerdoc draws the same page count as 26.2 for each. The text export holds the endnote text either way, so only the pixel check is affected.

The settings state w:defaultTabStop 65536, a default tab distance Word reads as zero. LibreOffice 24.2 imports it as 65536 twips, a 3,277 pt tab distance, so each of the ten 72 pt tabs after the centred '10' breaks the line, and the pinned PDF runs the paragraph over three pages, '10' alone on page two and 'Tabstops' on page three. The fix ('writerfilter: import PROP_TAB_STOP_DISTANCE 0', then 'as uInt16', master 2025-08) came with this sample and a test asserting one page before and after a round trip. broilerdoc draws one page.

Forty-five paragraphs fill most of page one; then a hidden paragraph names the Style1 page style with page number 5, and a table follows. The pinned 24.2 PDF has one page: the table follows paragraph 45 under the first page's 'first' header, and the page style change is lost. The fix ('do not skip empty page because of wrong page descriptor', master 2025-05-26, first released in 25.8) explains that Writer's initial layout put an automatic break before paragraph 26 and the manual break before the hidden paragraph, and that moving the content back skipped the page with the new style in SwFrame::WrongPageDesc, so the break was ignored. It came with this sample, whose table text says it must be after the page break, on a page with style Style1 and number 5, and a layout test that asserts it. broilerdoc draws the fixed layout: two pages, the table on the second under the 'first (Style1)' header. Cut-down copies converted with LibreOffice 24.2.7.2 show the defect depends on the page style: with a plain fo:break-before on the hidden paragraph instead, 24.2 does break the page. The text export holds the same text either way.
